decisive_items: excision of a dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans in the left inguinal–suprapubic region in 1998, with four local recurrences (2000, 2001, 2008, and 2009) treated surgically; she also received external radiotherapy (66 Gy) after the last excision

Fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the right lobe yielded a hemorrhagic background with isolated clusters of pleomorphic round and oval nuclei; it was classified as category IV/3, suspicious for primary or secondary malignancy
Contrast-enhanced CT of the neck and thorax confirmed a voluminous right thyroid mass and detected two pulmonary nodules consistent with metastases
response.rationale: The prior dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans with multiple recurrences and radiotherapy, combined with a thyroid FNA explicitly suspicious for secondary malignancy and pulmonary nodules consistent with metastases, strongly favors metastatic disease to the thyroid over a primary thyroid carcinoma.

rejected.why: Papillary thyroid carcinoma is possible but lacks classic cytologic features, lymphadenopathy, and does not explain the prior sarcoma history and pulmonary nodules as well as metastatic disease.

Anaplastic thyroid cancer could cause a large compressive thyroid mass with lung metastases, but the history of DFSP and FNA wording favoring primary or secondary malignancy make metastasis more likely.
Medullary thyroid carcinoma is not supported by calcitonin elevation, MEN features, or lymphadenopathy, and the prior sarcoma history is a stronger clue.
